## Master of Urbanism - Q1 Studio

Date: 3 September 2026 Duration: 8h

## Instructors

Daniele Cannatella, Daniela Maiullari, Rob van Houten, Ana Petrovic, Clementine Cottineau-Mugadza, Ines Zaid, Julia Fossa Marques (TA)

## Learning Objectives

- Understand what GIS is, and its role in urbanism
- Import vector, raster, tabular data
- Manipulate attribute tables
- Basic cartography (symbology, legend, layout)
- Targeted Analysis (density, spatial join, zonal statistics)

## Learning Outcomes

By the end of the workshop, students will be able to:

1.  Explain what GIS is and its role in urbanism; distinguish vector and raster data models (Understand)
2.  Import vector data and produce a basemap (Apply)
3.  Import raster data and produce a basemap (Apply)
4.  Manipulate attribute tables and produce a choropleth map (Apply)
5.  Perform a spatial join between point and polygon data and calculate density (Analyse)
6.  Compute and interpret basic descriptive and zonal statistics (Analyse)
7.  Apply cartographic principles (symbology, legend, layout) to produce one finished map (Apply/Analyse)

## Prerequisites

### Software

- **QGIS LTR 3.44** installed and running on every machine
- Shared **Miro board**, accessible to all students and staff, set up in advance
- **Excel** (or equivalent) available on every machine for the Part 4 barchart
- QGIS Plugins:
  - **QSM (Quick Map Service)**
  - **PDOK**

### Data

Download data from this **SurfDrive link**.
